entries.search: A measured score now sorts thousands of RAD51D repair changes A cell study scored 6,888 coding changes in RAD51D, a protein used when a break cuts both strands of DNA. entries.search: Senescent B cells gather in inflamed niches of COPD lungs A paper examined lung tissue from COPD patients and healthy controls, six per group, including smokers and non-smokers. entries.search: Seven small proteins tie a bacterial signal to spore-making Clostridioides difficile makes spores that let it persist and spread, and high levels of the signal c-di-GMP hold that process down. A Nature Communications paper finds a family of small membrane proteins whose genes are switched by c-di-GMP riboswitches. Raising one of them, CD1980.2, turned sporulation genes on and increased spores. Deleting all 7 genes left a severe sporulation defect, and adding still more c-di-GMP in that mutant did not push spores down any further. The newly published findings also draw attention to breastfeeding, where the researchers say evidence about GLP-1 exposure remains limited.
entries.title: GLP-1 prescribing rises among privately insured new US mothers

entries.summary: Swiss glaciers lost more than 5 per cent of their volume after a winter with little snow and an exceptionally warm summer. Even high mountain ice thinned sharply, while several small glaciers disappeared.

entries.search: US manufacturing stays in expansion as its input-price index jumps US manufacturing expanded for a ninth month in September, although its purchasing managers’ index slipped to 54.5. New orders and employment strengthened, while production growth eased and raw-material inventories moved back into contraction. The survey measures the breadth of monthly change, rather than percentage increases in prices or output. economics-markets Economics & Markets Economics 2026-10-01 Manufacturing expands for a ninth month More firms face higher input prices Orders strengthen while production eases US manufacturing keeps expanding as input price pressure rises Institute for Supply Management US manufacturing stays in expansion as its input-price index jumps Econ Data Tools

entries.search: VCN-01 pancreatic cancer trial leaves survival benefit uncertain A randomized phase 2b trial tested VCN-01 with chemotherapy in metastatic pancreatic cancer. Median survival was longer in the virus arm, but uncertainty in the analysis of everyone randomized included no benefit. A separately defined analysis group showed more favorable results. Fever, flu-like symptoms and other adverse effects were more common with the experimental virus. science Science Science 2026-10-01 The trial adds a virus to chemotherapy Survival estimates leave room for no benefit Fever and other adverse effects increased Pancreatic cancer trial leaves overall survival benefit uncertain Nature Medicine VIRAGE trial tests VCN-01 with chemotherapy in pancreatic cancer Theriva Biologics
entries.summary: A randomized phase 2b trial tested VCN-01 with chemotherapy in metastatic pancreatic cancer. Median survival was longer in the virus arm, but uncertainty in the analysis of everyone randomized included no benefit. A separately defined analysis group showed more favorable results. Fever, flu-like symptoms and other adverse effects were more common with the experimental virus.
entries.title: VCN-01 pancreatic cancer trial leaves survival benefit uncertain

entries.search: Westlothiana’s hidden gills overturn its reptile ancestry X-ray scans of Westlothiana lizziae, a Scottish fossil dating back 345 million years, revealed internal gills and a fish-like mouth. The anatomy moves the animal away from its familiar position near reptile ancestors and toward earlier relatives of four-limbed vertebrates. Its five digits and claw-like bones also complicate how scientists identify the earliest land-adapted animals from fossil footprints. science Science Science 2026-10-01 Scans reveal gills inside the fossil A fish-like mouth changes the family tree Claw-like feet complicate ancient trackways Hidden gills recast a Scottish fossil once placed near reptiles European Synchrotron Radiation Facility Westlothiana’s hidden anatomy revises its place among early vertebrates Scienmag
entries.summary: X-ray scans of Westlothiana lizziae, a Scottish fossil dating back 345 million years, revealed internal gills and a fish-like mouth. Its five digits and claw-like bones also complicate how scientists identify the earliest land-adapted animals from fossil footprints.
